en.title: UK Considers Banning Kids From Talking to Strangers in Fortnite, Roblox
en.summary: The UK government is exploring a significant new online safety measure that could prevent children from communicating with unknown adults in popular gaming platforms like Fortnite and Roblox. This potential ban stems from growing concerns over the exploitation of young players.
en.body:
The United Kingdom is reportedly considering a drastic step to enhance online safety for its younger citizens: a ban on children speaking to strangers within popular video games such as **Fortnite** and **Roblox**. This potential measure, discussed by the UK's online safety minister **Kanishka Narayan**, could extend existing social media restrictions to the interactive environments of online gaming.

Narayan's comments, made in conversation with The Sunday Times, revealed a primary concern following a visit to Australia, where similar social media bans are being implemented. The minister specifically cited "stranger pairing" – the ability for children to connect with unknown adults – as a significant danger. Notably, this issue was discussed more in the context of gaming platforms than traditional social media like TikTok or Instagram. "That will weigh quite significantly in my mind as we think about how we stop some of the most egregious harms for young people," Narayan stated.

## Protecting Young Players Online

These concerns have been echoed by **Rachel De Souza**, the Children's Commissioner for England. Speaking on Sky News, De Souza highlighted the particular vulnerability of young boys, who may spend significant time gaming rather than engaging on social media. "Boys often aren't on social media," De Souza explained. "They're often spending three or four hours a day gaming. And these games often have features that allow a 55-year-old in Arizona to come in and speak to a nine-year-old."

Platforms like **Roblox** have faced repeated scrutiny over their child safety protocols. The game has been the subject of numerous lawsuits concerning its ability to protect its predominantly young player base. In response to growing pressure and evolving UK law, some platforms, including **Roblox** and **Discord**, have already begun implementing age verification checks to help prevent children from interacting with adult strangers.

## What This Means for Gamers

If enacted, such a ban would represent a significant shift in how children can engage with online multiplayer games. The core appeal of titles like **Fortnite** and **Roblox** lies in their social aspects, allowing players to team up, strategize, and build communities with friends and sometimes, new acquaintances. Restricting communication could fundamentally alter the experience for millions of young players worldwide, potentially impacting player numbers and the very nature of these games.

The debate raises complex questions about parental responsibility, platform accountability, and the government's role in regulating children's digital lives. While the intention is clearly to protect children from exploitation, the practical implementation and potential unintended consequences for the gaming community are yet to be fully understood.

## What's Next

The UK government is expected to continue its review of online safety measures in the coming months. Details regarding the specific scope and enforcement of any potential ban on in-game communication for children have not yet been announced.

es.title: Reino Unido considera prohibir a los niños hablar con desconocidos en Fortnite y Roblox
es.summary: El gobierno del Reino Unido está explorando una medida de seguridad en línea significativa que podría impedir a los niños comunicarse con adultos desconocidos en plataformas de juegos populares como Fortnite y Roblox. Esta potencial prohibición surge de crecientes preocupaciones sobre el abuso de jugadores jóvenes.
es.body:
El Reino Unido está considerando un paso drástico para mejorar la seguridad en línea para sus ciudadanos más jóvenes: una prohibición para que los niños hablen con desconocidos dentro de juegos de video populares como **Fortnite** y **Roblox**. Esta medida potencial, discutida por el ministro de seguridad en línea **Kanishka Narayan**, podría extender las restricciones existentes de las redes sociales a los entornos interactivos de los juegos en línea.

Narayan comentó que su principal preocupación sigue un viaje a Australia, donde se están implementando restricciones similares en las redes sociales. El ministro citó específicamente la "pareja desconocida" – la capacidad de los niños para conectarse con adultos desconocidos – como un peligro significativo. Esta cuestión se discutió más en el contexto de las plataformas de juegos que en las redes sociales tradicionales como TikTok o Instagram. "Eso pesará bastante en mi mente cuando pensemos en cómo podemos detener algunos de los daños más graves para los jóvenes", afirmó Narayan.

## Protegiendo a los jugadores jóvenes en línea

Estas preocupaciones han sido repetidas por **Rachel De Souza**, la Comisionada de Niños para Inglaterra. Al hablar en Sky News, De Souza resaltó la vulnerabilidad particular de los niños, especialmente los chicos, que pueden pasar horas jugando en lugar de interactuar en las redes sociales. "Los niños a menudo no están en las redes sociales", explicó De Souza. "Están pasando tres o cuatro horas al día jugando. Y estos juegos a menudo tienen características que permiten a un hombre de 55 años en Arizona hablar con un niño de nueve años".

Plataformas como **Roblox** han enfrentado repetidas críticas por sus protocolos de seguridad para niños. El juego ha sido objeto de numerosas demandas legales debido a su capacidad para proteger a su base de jugadores predominantemente jóvenes. En respuesta a la creciente presión y la evolución de la ley del Reino Unido, algunas plataformas, incluyendo **Roblox** y **Discord**, han comenzado a implementar verificaciones de edad para ayudar a prevenir que los niños interactúen con desconocidos adultos.

## ¿Qué significa esto para los jugadores?

Si se implementa, tal prohibición representaría un cambio significativo en cómo los niños pueden interactuar con juegos de video en línea multijugador. El atractivo central de títulos como **Fortnite** y **Roblox** reside en sus aspectos sociales, permitiendo a los jugadores unirse, estrategizar y construir comunidades con amigos y, a veces, nuevos conocidos. Restringir la comunicación podría alterar fundamentalmente la experiencia para millones de jugadores jóvenes en todo el mundo, potencialmente afectando el número de jugadores y la naturaleza misma de estos juegos.

La discusión plantea cuestiones complejas sobre la responsabilidad parental, la rendición de cuentas de la plataforma y el papel del gobierno en la regulación de las vidas digitales de los niños. Si bien la intención es claramente proteger a los niños del abuso, la implementación práctica y las posibles consecuencias no deseadas para la comunidad de juegos aún no se han comprendido plenamente.

## Próximos pasos

El gobierno del Reino Unido está esperando continuar la revisión de las medidas de seguridad en línea en los próximos meses. Los detalles sobre el alcance específico y la aplicación de cualquier prohibición potencial sobre la comunicación en juego para niños aún no han sido anunciados.

content_raw: A possible social media ban for children in the UK could be expanded to games, the government's online safety minister has suggested. Speaking to The Sunday Times (via Game Developer ) Kanishka Narayan said that a ban on social media for teenagers—which is being considered by the UK following a social media ban being implemented in Australia—could include restrictions for online video game platforms like Roblox and Fortnite, an area that Australia's social media ban does not extend to. Narayan didn't cite any specific games in his conversation with The Sunday Times, but he said that, following a recent visit to Australia, his primary concern regarding children's use of the Internet was over "stranger pairing", between children and adults they don't know. Apparently, this issue was discussed, "mostly in the context of gaming platforms" rather than conventional social media like Tiktok, Instagram etc. "That will weigh quite significantly in my mind as we think about how we stop some of the most egregious harms for young people," Narayan added. Narayan's statements were recently echoed on Sky News by Rachel De Souza, the Children's Commissioner for England. Speaking on Sunday Morning with Trevor Phillips, De Souza said that young boys in particular are vulnerable to being exploited on gaming platforms. "Boys often aren't on social media," De Souza said. "They're often spending three or four hours a day gaming. And these games often have features that allow a 55-year-old in Arizona to come in and speak to a nine-year-old." (Image credit: Roblox) Roblox in particular has been repeatedly called out for its failures to adequately protect its player-base—which is largely composed of children. The platform has been subject to numerous lawsuits over child safety concerns, while there have been "at least two dozen" people arrested in the US and accused of "abducting or abusing victims" they'd met on Roblox. Roblox's responses to these lawsuits and allegations have varied in quality , but this month, the company will introduce new age-based account categories as it strives to "more closely align content access, communication settings and parental controls with a user's age." These are much-needed and long overdue features, though it's worth noting that this is only one reason why Roblox has been accused of putting its audience at risk of exploitation. But is a wider social media ban that incorporates games the answer? Well, in March, the BBC reported that the effectiveness of Australia's social media ban had been questioned, with the country's Internet regulator saying that social media companies were not doing enough to comply with it. In response, a spokesperson for Meta said that the company was "committed to complying" with the ban, while claiming that accurate age determination was "a challenge for the whole industry."
